description: GSA Public Buildings Service The U.S. Government is seeking competitive lease proposals for new and/or continuing leasing opportunities through the Leasing Portal. Award under this RLP will be made to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable negotiated offer. City: Lewiston State: Idaho Delineated Area: City limits of Lewiston Minimum ABOA Square Feet: 3,784 ABOA SF Maximum ABOA Square Feet: 4,162 ABOA SF Space Type: Office, Retail Parking: 0 Lease Term: Full Term: 15 Years Firm Term: 10 Years Firm Amortization Term: 10 years for both Tenant Improvements and Building Specific Amortized Capital. AGENCY UNIQUE REQUIREMENTS Agency Tenant Improvement Allowance: $53.65 per ABOA SF Building Specific Amortized Capital (BSAC): $12.00 per ABOA SF Additional Requirements: One (1) public transportation stop must be located within 1,600 walkable linear feet of the building�s public entrance. Space must not be on the same property as establishments primarily involved in the sale of alcohol or the sale and discharge of firearms. Minimum 20 feet column spacing (center-on-center) and from any interior wall. Must be one (1) contiguous space on a single floor with no interior steps, ramps, and cannot be separated by any common areas. Any space being offered for consideration that is not located on the ground floor must provide two elevators (One passenger and one freight elevator). Space must be no more than twice as long as wide. If applicable, provide history or all history of water/moisture intrusion or mold; must provide remediation history and evidence of remediation, including source corrections, repeated issues or interference with tenant�s quiet enjoyment may result in disqualification. 24/7/365 temperature-controlled server room Must provide the Government with parking that meets or exceeds all applicable local zoning requirements. Security Level II HOW TO OFFER Unless otherwise authorized by the LCO or his/her designated representative, offers may only be submitted electronically to GSA using the Requirement Specific Acquisition Platform (RSAP) located at https://leasing.gsa.gov. RSAP enables Offerors to electronically offer space for lease to the Federal Government. The offer submission process is web-enabled, allowing all registered participants to submit and update offers to lease space to the Government in response to a single RLP for a specific space requirement. Lease awards will be made to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable offer without negotiations. Offered space must comply with all applicable Federal, State, and Local jurisdiction requirements, including standards for fire and life safety, accessibility, seismic resilience, and energy efficiency. In order to be considered for award, offers conforming to the requirements of the RLP shall be submitted through LOP/RSAP no later than October 2, 2026, 5:00 PM PDT. Offerors must submit all documentation identified in this RLP using RSAP. RSAP generates the Lessor's Annual Cost Statement (GSA Form 1217) and Proposal to Lease Space (GSA Form 1364) based on the Offeror�s inputs to the online workflow. These auto-populated forms are available for review on the attachments page of the RSAP workflow and are automatically included as part of the offer upon submission; there is no need for the Offeror to manually complete the attached blank version of these two forms. Offerors can revise the auto-generated GSA Form 1217 and/or GSA Form 1364 by changing the inputs to the online workflow. Any subsequent revisions to offer documents must be submitted through RSAP. There is no paper-based submission process under this RLP and paper submissions will not be considered, unless otherwise authorized by the LCO. IMPORTANT NOTES Check the attachments and links section of this notice for possible, additional project-specific requirements or modifications to the RLP. Please review Section 889 of the FY19 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) regarding telecommunications equipment restrictions: https://acquisition.gov/FAR-Case-2019-009/889_Part_B SAM registration should be initiated as soon as possible. Refer to RLP Section 3.04, subparagraph N. The Government may award multiple leases to satisfy new requirements or to compete expiring leases. Specific requirements will be identified following the close of the Open Period. Subleases will not be considered. Submission by anyone other than the owner or manager of a property must be accompanied by written consent from the ownership granting authority to the representative in providing the information to the Government.

title: Germany – Purchase of CO2 emission credits – Dynamic Purchasing System for the Offsetting of the ECB's Greenhouse Gas Emissions
description: Since 2010, the ECB implements an environmental management system (EMS) in accordance with the international standard ISO 14001:2015 and Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2017/1505 and 2018/2026. The priority of the ECB remains to prevent greenhouse gas emissions wherever possible, limiting emissions in areas in which they cannot be avoided. Where emissions cannot be further limited and as greenhouse gas emissions cannot currently be reduced to zero, the ECB decided to offset its greenhouse gas emissions expressed in tonnes of CO2 equivalent as a complementary measure to its mitigation efforts (2021: 16 023,2 tonnes of CO2). The ECB envisages launching a dynamic purchasing system with a duration of initially two years, extendable at the ECB's option by another two years (total duration up to four years).

title: FAA Industry Engagement Event - Oct 13-15, 2026 - Aviation Spectrum Interference Detection Solutions - Early Registration Required
description: ****Registration for the Unclassified portion of the FAA Industry Engagement Event has been extended until Friday, October 2nd at 11:59 EST. Please register at the link.**** **Announcement has been edited to correct the numbering within the Announcement** FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION (FAA) Request for Information PROGRAM TITLE: Aviation Spectrum Interference Detection Solution Name: Gilbert Park, FAA Contracting Officer Organization: AAQ-740, Training & Aviation Acquisition Branch Region: FAA Headquarters Phone Number: (405) 954-7898 Email: gilbert.n.park@faa.gov Industry Engagement Day: 13 October 2026 Vendor One-on-One Sessions: 14-15 October 2026 Registration Deadline: 2 October 2026 Procurement Method: Request for Information (RFI) II. Introduction/Purpose The FAA is hosting an Industry Engagement Event for a Spectrum Interference Detection Solution for the following purposes: Communicate emerging need to industry for a new mission capability resulting from unprecedented spectrum utilization, requests, auctions, and technology proliferation. Provide background, historical events, and use case vision to inform industry about the FAA�s interference detection capability gaps and inquire about possible solutions and technologies necessary to detect and locate spectrum interference in any one of the bands utilized for aviation. Gather information to assess the availability of solution(s). Registration will include a response to a short list of survey questions that one designated participant per vendor company will need to upload. Conduct follow-up with vendors, as needed, to understand RFI responses. Assess industry interest and availability of solutions among vendors and determine where challenges exist in producing the needed capabilities for such a system. The FAA will use the information from vendor responses during event registration to assist in determining any future phases of market investigation and engagement. The FAA does not commit to an acquisition with this notice. II. Background Interested parties are advised that: This is not a Request for Proposals; The FAA is not seeking unsolicited proposals; The FAA will not pay for any information received or costs incurred in registering for, participation in, or attendance at the main Industry Engagement Event or Vendor One-on-One Sessions; Any costs associated with responding to survey questions as part of the event registration are incurred solely at the submitting party�s expense; FAA, at its sole discretion, may contact one, some, all, or none of the Industry Engagement Day registrants and ask for additional information; and Vendor participation in any informational session is not a promise for future business with the FAA. Do not include any sensitive or classified information in your Industry Engagement event registration responses to this RFI. This RFI in no way alters the FAA�s obligations under existing law, including any duties owed by the FAA under the Freedom of Information Act. III. Solution Objectives The FAA seeks to understand industry interest and capabilities to modernize and accelerate the real-time detection, characterization, and reporting of interference affecting spectrum-dependent aviation systems. Potential solutions should proactively monitor the radio frequency (RF) environment and, to the greatest extent practicable, detect, identify, characterize, geolocate, and alert on RF interference, jamming, spoofing, and other anomalous conditions that could degrade aviation communications, navigation, surveillance, or other spectrum-dependent aviation capabilities. The ideal solution will continuously monitor RF activity relevant to aviation operations, collect and analyze spectrum metrics and system performance data to identify abnormal or unauthorized emissions, correlate information across multiple sensors, platforms, and geographic locations, and provide timely reporting to support rapid assessment and mitigation. Desired capabilities include signal detection and classification, emitter characterization, geolocation where feasible, waveform and protocol analysis, trend analysis, and identification of potential interference sources and contributing factors. The solution should collect, retain, and report data to enable timely operational response by the FAA, as well as short-term operational assessments and long-term trend analysis. The solution should identify and visualize interference, congestion, and other RF activity patterns over time and across geographic locations. Historical data should be retained in a searchable repository and support flexible querying, export, visualization, and reporting. The solution should support post-event analysis by correlating RF conditions with aircraft operations and other relevant operational data, where available. The FAA is interested in solutions applicable across the National Airspace System (NAS), including airport surface, terminal, and enroute environments; continental United States (CONUS) and outside the continental United States (OCONUS); domestic and oceanic operations; and both ground-based and airborne systems. The system should be able to monitor all aviation frequencies in use (illustrated in the Attachment in Section V). Solutions should be capable of supporting scalable deployment across distributed sensor networks while providing centralized data aggregation, analysis, and visualization. The FAA seeks to understand the stage of evolution of proposed solutions, including whether they are in the design, development, implementation, integration, operational, or commercially deployable phase. Respondents should also identify the role(s) they envision, such as technology developer, systems integrator, service provider, or system operator. IV. Events Industry Engagement Day 1: This day will include presentations by the FAA to describe the FAA interest and objectives for an aviation spectrum interference detection solution. Presentation topics include current aviation spectrum environment and interference challenges, FAA vision and exploration of potential solutions, and desired technical capabilities (monitoring, detection, analytics, data, architecture, and integration). The FAA is interested in feedback on potential acquisition solutions and the possibility of purchasing as a service. The first portion of the day will be open to all registrants and available in-person or online, while the second portion will be classified at the Secret level and restricted to registrants with a Secret Clearance and in-person only. The event will be held at The MITRE Corporation in McLean, VA. Vendor One-on-One Sessions (Days 2 and 3): The FAA may invite vendors to attend a One-On-One Session, either unclassified (in-person or virtual) or classified at the Secret level (in-person only). Sessions with individual vendors will be scheduled at the discretion of the FAA, based on vendor survey responses included in the event registration. If requested to provide additional information, brief vendor presentations are encouraged and vendors should expect discussion and questions from the FAA regarding their solution(s). The sessions will be held at The MITRE Corporation in McLean, VA. V. Attachment FAA Frequency Bands Poster � Radio Frequency Bands Supporting Aviation IV. General Instructions A. Questions Any questions regarding this request for information must be submitted in writing by 18 September 2026. Please send question(s) to Mr. Park, at the POC information in the header of this announcement. Respondents are prohibited from providing classified information in their questions on this notice. The FAA will provide answers to selected questions during the Industry Engagement Day 1. DO NOT INCLUDE CLASSIFIED INFORMATION IN THE SURVEY RESPONSES. B. Registration All attendees (virtual or in-person) wishing to participate in any portion of the event must complete a registration format *****REGISTRATION URL: https://na.eventscloud.com/8882

title: F/A-18E/F Infrared Search and Track (IRST) FPU-13/A Fuel Tank Assembly (FTA) Technical Data Package (TDP)
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), 47123 Buse Road, Patuxent River, MD 20670, intends to award a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract to The Boeing Company, St. Louis, MO, on a sole source basis. This contract will provide a tailored Technical Data Package (TDP) for the FPU-13/A Fuel Tank Assembly (FTA) to support repair and sustainment activities, as well as the hosting and support of TDP Guidance Conferences and incremental In-Process Reviews (IPRs). As the prime contractor responsible for the overall system development, architecture, and integration of the Infrared Search and Track (IRST) system onto the F/A-18 aircraft, The Boeing Company uniquely possesses the comprehensive knowledge, experience, and technical data required to successfully develop and deliver the FPU-13/A FTA TDP. Consequently, an award to any other source would result in unacceptable delays in meeting the Navy�s operational requirements and a substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition. The authority permitting other than full and open competition is Title 10, U.S. Code 3204(a)(1), as implemented by the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1, "Only One Responsible Source" and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. This synopsis is for informational purposes only and is not a request for competitive proposals. Interested parties may identify their interest and capability by responding to this synopsis. The Government will consider all capability information received prior to the closing date. There is no commitment by the Government to issue any solicitation, make an award, or be responsible for any monies expended by any interested party before award of a contract for the efforts detailed above. Information provided herein in no way binds the Government to solicit for or award a contract. In addition to this pre-solicitation notice, the Government has also issued a sources sought notice to determine if any other sources have the potential to fulfill this requirement. Any responses to the sources sought will be reviewed and may impact the Government's acquisition decisions as they relate to this requirement. If you have any questions regarding this synopsis, please contact Gabrielle Blew at gabrielle.j.blew.civ@us.navy.mil or Jessica Myers at jessica.v.myers.civ@us.navy.mil. For small business or subcontracting opportunities, contact The Boeing Company at joseph.l.unger@boeing.com.

description: 1. Synopsis & Purpose The Uncrewed Aircraft System Program Management Office is releasing this Request for Whitepapers (RFW) in support of the BDE UAS Prototype Project. A fully executed and signed Consortium Vendor Agreement (CVA). An active SAM.gov registration, Unique Entity Identification (UEI) number, and active WAWF registration. Interested vendors must first apply for consortium membership by submitting an application to DMConsortium@army.mil. 3. title: Heavy Equipment Rental Services
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), the Management and Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy-owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from qualified vendors capable of providing heavy equipment rental services to support laboratory operations at INL facilities in Idaho Falls and at Site locations west of Idaho Falls. BACKGROUND INL utilizes outside vendors to obtain equipment that is unavailable through the Central Facilities Area (CFA) equipment pool or required for specialized tasks. Timely access to safe, compliant, and well-maintained equipment is essential to maintaining project schedules and mitigating risk. Heavy equipment rentals enable BEA to meet operational needs without long-term capital purchases. Proposed base period: January 1, 2027 � December 31, 2027, with four (4) option years extending through December 31, 2031. SCOPE OF WORK Responding vendors must be capable of furnishing heavy equipment rental services on an as-needed basis, including delivery and pickup when requested by BEA. The rental fleet should encompass the following representative, non-limiting categories typically required by BEA, including but not limited to: � Rollers 79-in. & 84-in. double-drum; 84-in. padfoot 12-16 ton class; 84-in. smooth 13-17 ton class; 68-in. pneumatic 14 � 16 ton class � Soil compactors (Heavy-duty, suitable for earthwork and compaction operations.) � Dozers Medium-class with low ground pressure; Medium-class high-track configuration; Large-Class; Extra-large-class � Motor graders Heavy-duty suitable for road construction, maintenance & finish grading) � Excavators and attachments Hydraulic excavators including long-reach 35-ton to 40 ton class, 74-ton class, 90-ton class; Hydraulic Hammer attachments compatible with 36 � 40-ton hydraulic excavator, or 49- to 52-ton hydraulic excavator; Rotary cutters compatible with 36 � 40-ton hydraulic excavator; Multi-processor attachment compatible with 49- to 52-ton hydraulic excavator � Scrapers Heavy-duty self propelled and/or tandem-engine scraper suitable for large-scale earthmoving operations. � Articulated haul trucks (30-ton payload and/or 45-ton payload capacity) � Wheel loaders (Medium-production and/or large-or extra-large production) Fork attachment compatible with the proposed wheel loader; approx. 72-in and 96-in fork lengths � Water equipment (12K gal. watertower, water trucks with 6K gal. and/or 8K gal.) � Rubber track dump trucks (suitable for operation on soft ground or uneven terrain) Equipment furnished shall meet or exceed OSHA, ANSI, and applicable manufacturer maintenance standards; be delivered in safe, good working condition; and include required documentation (inspection records, manuals, tags, capacity charts). PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested firms are requested to provide expressions of interest submitted to chase.egbert@Inl.gov by close-of business on 02 Oct. 2026. Responses must include sufficient written information confirming the responder�s qualifications and interest. Company name and point of contact. NAICS and business size classification Description of rental fleet and capability to supply equipment in the categories listed above, including typical makes/models and availability windows. Delivery and pickup capabilities for INL locations; standard lead times; emergency response capability. Standard equipment delivery timelines should not exceed one-week from the date of request. Repair or replacement of malfunctioning or defective equipment should occur within 24-hours of notification. Maintenance, inspection, and documentation practices; sample service/inspection records. Repair and replacement response commitments (e.g., 24-hour repair/replace) and onsite service coverage. Safety, security, and compliance: confirmation of OSHA/ANSI compliance; onsite requirements (REAL ID; Foreign National Access Program approvals when applicable; BEA escort compliance). Quality program certifications and applicable regulatory compliance (e.g., DOT for transport). Standard rental terms (hourly/daily/weekly/monthly) and pricing structures; discount schedules or IDIQ approaches (note: detailed pricing may be requested in a subsequent RFP). References for similar heavy equipment rental support to government or industrial sites. Note that responses must be no more than fifteen (15) pages in length in PDF format. Only select respondents, as determined by BEA, will receive an invitation to participate in the anticipated RFP solicitation. PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents must mark information in their responses accordingly.

description: În contextul procesului continuu de modernizare și dezvoltare a infrastructurii medicale, autoritatea contractantă urmărește încheierea unui acord-cadru având ca obiect furnizarea de echipamente și dispozitive medicale, în vederea creșterii calității serviciilor medicale oferite în cadrul Spitalului de Obstetrica Ginecologie (SPOG) Buftea,Ilfov. title: FCCD-ACM-MJ Support Services
description: Introduction/Background The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Armaments Center (DEVCOM AC) Munitions Engineering Technology Center (METC), Medium and Cannon Caliber Munitions Division FCDD-ACM-MJ at Picatinny Arsenal, NJ is issuing this sources sought notice to conduct market research to determine the ability to perform complete life cycle engineering for a wide variety of munition systems across DEVCOM AC for various customers. This includes exploratory, advanced and engineering development, experimental testing, quality engineering, evaluation and qualification of munition systems and component concepts, as well as production and manufacturing engineering for munition systems and components. 2.Disclaimer THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A �REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP)� TO BE SUBMITTED. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. RESPONSES WILL NOT BE RETURNED TO THE RESPONDER. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) OR RFP, IF ANY ISSUED. IF A SOLICITATION IS RELEASED, IT WILL BE SYNOPSIZED ON THE GOVERNMENT-WIDE POINT OF ENTRY (GPE). IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THE GPE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT. 3.Requirements: 3.1 The Contractor shall provide qualified engineering professionals to perform comprehensive engineering functions supporting the research, design, development, test and evaluation, production, and sustainment of advanced munition systems. The Contractor shall apply engineering competencies to solve complex technical challenges throughout the munition system lifecycle by executing rigorous engineering activities. The Contractor shall apply core engineering disciplines by executing critical technical activities such as performing requirements decomposition and system architecture design; creating detailed Computer-Aided Design (CAD) models; conducting structural, thermal, and kinematic finite element analysis (FEA); designing analog and digital circuit boards; developing embedded software and control algorithms; and formulating developmental test plans alongside post-test data reduction. Through these tasks, the Contractor shall deliver engineering artifacts such as Interface Control Documents (ICDs), Technical Data Packages (TDPs), simulation reports, and software version descriptions and actively participate in formal/informal reviews to ensure robust engineering rigor, standard methodologies, and scientific discipline are applied to the development, production, and sustainment of the munition systems. They will review designs and Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs) against military and commercial specifications, Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) standards, and producibility standards and proactively identifying opportunities to reduce costs, accelerate schedules, optimize manufacturing processes, and elevate overall quality. Throughout the life cycle, the contractor shall be responsible for supporting project preparation encompassing planning, cost analysis, scheduling, facility coordination, and integration. Finally, they shall be responsible for collaborating with multi-disciplinary program teams to support the reliable delivery and sustained performance of munition systems, aligning all efforts with operational utility and organizational mission requirements. 3.2 The individuals are expected to travel on a semi-regular basis. 3.3 The Contractor shall attend, support, and report on meetings, review documents, contribute to the preparation of original documents, analyze cost, performance, risk, and provide recommendations or courses of action and ensure objectives are met. 3.4 The Contractor shall support the generation and review of briefing materials. 3.5 The Contractor shall support, coordinate, participate, and record regular Integrated Product Team (IPT) meetings on assigned projects/programs. 3.6 The Contractor shall provide technical advice regarding project feasibility, definitions of project scope, complexities/risk involved, phases required, and time schedules. 3.7 The Contractor shall keep project team leads/ Armaments Project Officer (APO) and Branch and Division supervisors informed of program/project status, issues, problems and recommendations through oral communication, proper documentation including trip reports and attendance at regularly scheduled and informal meetings. Provide technical support and advice to project team leads/APOs and Branch and Division supervisors on engineering aspects of assigned munition systems. This shall include solution recommendations regarding major problems and conflicting requirements with assigned projects/programs. 4. Background The applicable NAICS code for this requirement is 541330 Engineering Services and the PSC code is R425 Engineering and Technical Services. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capability statement. 5. Submission Details Interested contractors are strongly encouraged to submit a capabilities statement with the following information: 5.1 Ability to provide a product that meets the above specifications. 5.2 Historical information demonstrating that you have the ability to provide the product (contract number(s), dollar value(s), Point of Contacts, and brief description of work performed). 5.3 In addition, please provide full company name and address, point of contact with telephone number and email address, CAGE Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, size of business (i.e. large, small, disadvantaged, veteran owned, woman owned, etc.) and applicable NAICS, Product Service Code (PSC), and website (if applicable). All data should be provided at no cost to the US Government by October 3, 2026 at 3PM EDT. 5.4 Contractors must be properly registered in the Government System for Award Management database (SAM). Contractors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation of requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220, or via the Internet at www.sam.gov. 5.5 This is a market survey for information only and shall not be construed as a request for a proposal or as an obligation on the part of the US Government. The US Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this market survey or otherwise pay for information solicited. 5.6 The official response must be submitted to: The US Army Contracting Command - Rock Island at Picatinny, ATTN: Contracting/Agreements Officer: Charlotte Sylvain-Ceraul, charlotte.a.sylvain-ceraul.civ@army.mil and Contract Specialist: Qendresa Neza, qendresa.neza.civ@army.mil. Phone inquiries will not be addressed; all requests should be submitted in writing via email. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the survey.

title: Notice of Intent - BPA for Language Services
description: This Notice is not a call for sources, quotes, or solicitations. The deadline for response is 1700 EDT on October 3, 2026. Responses may be directed by e-mail to Angelika Graham, Contracting Officer, Office of Language Services, Department of State. Any technical or other information received in response to this Notice will be considered for the sole purpose of market research for future requirements. The Office of Language Services of the U.S. Department of State contracts directly with qualified individuals to provide foreign language interpreting, translating, and related services in support of diplomatic and foreign affairs activities at the highest levels of the U.S. Government. The Office has limited contracting authority pursuant to Department of State Acquisition Regulations (DOSAR), the Foreign Affairs Manual (FAM), and FAR Part 13 to contract for interpreters and translators domestically. DOSAR 601.601-70 further defines this as the authority �to enter into and administer simplified acquisition transactions under FAR Part 13 and orders against existing contracts up to the maximum ordering threshold or limitation for interpreting, translating, conference reporting, and related language support and escort services.� The Office establishes fixed rates of payment for specific language services each fiscal year on the basis of market research. In accordance with industry standards, these rates are not published for the general public. For the purposes of this Notice, the term �qualified� describes those individuals who have passed the Office of Language Services test(s) of interpreting and translating skill for one or more foreign languages and have successfully provided language services under a Blanket Purchase Agreement or Purchase Order with the Office of Language Services in the past. In accordance with 6 FAM 1550, the Office develops and administers examinations to evaluate the interpreting and translating skills of prospective direct-hire and contract staff. These exams are offered by invitation only subject to the needs of the Department. Individual members of the public who wish to be considered as test candidates should visit https://www.state.gov/freelance-linguists-ols/ to view criteria and application information. In addition, qualified bidders must hold U.S. citizenship or permanent resident status and have active contractor profiles in the System for Award Management (SAM). They must also be able to obtain and maintain a Moderate or High-risk Public Trust Certification from the State Department�s Office of Personnel Suitability and Security. They must agree to accept our fixed rates of payment for specific language services. Finally, they are forbidden from subcontracting and must adhere to strict professional standards. The Office of Language Services intends to issue Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPA) for Language Services to qualified bidders effective October 1, 2026. The Office anticipates that roughly 850 Agreements with individual foreign language translators, interpreters, and specialists will be issued. The value of calls against these individual Agreements will not exceed $350,000, with no individual call to exceed $25,000 and over half of all calls at or below the micro purchase threshold $15,000. There is no guarantee of assignment under these Agreements. The anticipated total combined annual value of all calls against all of these Agreements is between $20 million and $30 million. Individual BPA calls are awarded at the discretion of the Language Services Contracting Officer, based on recommendations from Subject Matter Experts within the Office and factors including evaluated skill sets, prior performance, and availability to accept the assignment.

title: Finland – Diagnostic devices – Diffuusiokapasiteetti/Spirometrialaitteistot
description: Hankinnan kohteena on Etelä-Savon hyvinvointialueen (Eloisa) Mikkelin keskussairaalaan tuleva diffuusiokapasiteetti-/spirometrialaitteisto (1 kpl) sekä laitekohtaiset kulutustarvikkeet, ohjelmisto, lisenssit ja huoltopalvelu. Hankinnassa on lisäksi optio kahdelle (2) vastaavanlaiselle laitekokonaisuudelle (diffuusiokapasiteetti-/spirometrialaitteistot) sekä yhdelle (1) spirometrialaitteistolle. Eloisa päättää mahdollisten optioiden hankkimisesta vuoden 2028 loppuun mennessä. Sopimuskausi alkaa sopimuksen allekirjoittamisesta. Sopimus allekirjoitetaan mahdollisimman pian lainvoimaisen päätöksen jälkeen. Sopimus on toistaiseksi voimassa oleva. Laitteen tulee soveltua diffuusiokapasiteetin mittaamiseen ja spirometriatutkimusten tekemiseen. Spirometria ja diffuusiokapasiteetti ovat keskeisiä keuhkojen toimintakokeita. Spirometrialla mitataan keuhkojen tilavuutta ja ilman virtausta, mikä auttaa tunnistamaan ahtauttavat (esim. astma, COPD) tai rajoittavat keuhkosairaudet. Diffuusiokapasiteetti mittaa kaasujen siirtymistä keuhkorakkuloista vereen, ja sitä käytetään keuhkokudoksen sairauksien (esim. fibroosi) arvioinnissa. Laitteella tulee pystyä tekemään spirometria ja bronkodilataatiokoe, diffuusiokoe hengityslihasvoiman mittaus sekä SNIP. Pyydettäessä tarjoaja toimittaa kustannuksellaan tarjotun laitteistokokonaisuuden koekäyttöön Mikkelin keskussairaalalle. Tarjouspyyntö julkaistaan ehdollisena optioiden osalta: optioiden hankinnat voidaan toteuttaa, mikäli hankinnoille varatut investointimäärärahat hyväksytään.

title: Sole Source Justification JA-2026-03-8045 - TSA STIP SETA Bridge Support
description: This sole-source justification provides authority to award a task order on the basis of other than full and open competition for Systems Engineering and Technical Assistance (SETA) support services. The contractor will perform SETA services to assist the SC Security Technology Integration Program (STIP) in system development and operations and maintenance (O&M). This includes providing technical guidance throughout the acquisition lifecycle and systems engineering life cycle (SELC), reviewing open architecture (OA), System of Systems (SoS), design documentation, and supporting risk management activities. The contractor will also assist in developing and maintaining documentation, reviewing operational processes for compliance and efficiency, supporting incident response and troubleshooting, and execution of major initiatives within STIP and related security technology efforts. These services will ensure accurate reporting and device connectivity to TSANetwork (TSANet) via the Security Technology Information eXchange (STIX) for alarm counts and throughput data. The contractor will validate the accuracy and integrity of system-generated reports, support improvements to reporting tools, and ensure compliance with Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and TSA data standards. Additionally, the contractor will review and validate device integration with TSANet, verify data transmission protocols, and assist in resolving connectivity issues to ensure reliable data collection and aggregation. STIP is the interface of Secure Flight (SF), Credential Authentication Technology CAT 2 (CAT-2), enhanced metal detectors (EMDs), and connectivity of other Transportation Security Equipment (TSE). These TSEs enhance the capabilities necessary to sustain TSA�s mission-critical operations, equip the frontline, and safeguard the traveling public. STIP provides the connection between TSEs located in airports and the TSANet for sharing of mission, and operational and maintenance data. Specifically, STIP enables network connectivity for exchanging the near-real time passenger vetting status of more than 1.7 million passengers daily between TSA�s SF system and over 2,100 CAT / CAT-2 units deployed at airports across the country. Without a STIP connection, that data cannot be shared with the checkpoints and data is performed manually by Transportation Security Officers (TSOs) on an hourly basis. SETA support services are paramount to providing technical monitoring of the STIP platform including analysis of vulnerabilities to the system and identification of process improvements and efficiencies to current and continuous operational changes. Only B&B can provide the required continuity of services with the highest level of confidence while maintaining support for active and time-sensitive SC initiatives and operations and maintenance services. These SC initiatives include ensuring successful management and completion of Advanced Imaging Technology (AIT) connectivity, Security Technology Information eXchange (STIX) connectivity, and operational utility evaluation (OUE) activities by November 2026; ensuring successful management and completion of the STIP database server migration to Windows Server 19 by January 2027; ensuring successful completion and operational readiness of the Data Center 15 (DC15) development lab by March 2027; and ensuring successful management and completion of ongoing STIP engineering change requests (ECRs), enhancements, and O&M. +++++++++++++

Vidare ska upphandlingen säkra att tjänsterna utförs kostnadseffektivt, med lägsta möjliga miljöpåverkan och med ett gott kundbemötande. Entreprenaden omfattar: - Hämtning av förpackningar - Hämtning av wellpapp - Hämtning av emballageplast, säck - Hämtning av tidningar/returpapper och sekretess - Hämtning av pant och returförpackningar - Hämtning av metallavfall - Hämtning av textilavfall och textilgåvor som inte utgör kommunalt avfall - Hämtning av elavfall - Hämtning av grovavfall (uttjänta möbler, cyklar, leksaker, mattor och dylikt) - Hämtning av bygg- och rivningsavfall - Hämtning av träavfall (rester från träslöjd eller träpallar) - - Hämtning av trädgårdsavfall - - Hämtning av farligt avfall (ljuskällor och lysrör, batterier, stickande eller skärande material, kemikalier, läkemedel, färg, trycksatta behållare, tryckimpregnerat trä med mera) - - Inrapportering av farligt avfall till Naturvårdsverket - Hyra och köp av kärl och behållare (option) - - Tvätt av kärl och behållare - Rengöring och tillsyn av soprum/miljörum - Behandling av grovavfall, trä, metall, trädgårdsavfall Entreprenaden omfattar fastland och öar med broförbindelse i hela kommunen. Entreprenaden är inte föremål för anbudsräkning i egen regi. Entreprenören ansvarar för kundtjänst, registerhållning och fakturering av avfallsavgifter till varje avropande part. title: Diffuusiokapasiteetti/Spirometrialaitteistot
description: Diffuusiokapasiteetti/Spirometrialaitteistot Hankinnan kohteena on Etelä-Savon hyvinvointialueen (Eloisa) Mikkelin keskussairaalaan tuleva diffuusiokapasiteetti-/spirometrialaitteisto (1 kpl) sekä laitekohtaiset kulutustarvikkeet, ohjelmisto, lisenssit ja huoltopalvelu. Hankinnassa on lisäksi optio kahdelle (2) vastaavanlaiselle laitekokonaisuudelle (diffuusiokapasiteetti-/spirometrialaitteistot) sekä yhdelle (1) spirometrialaitteistolle. Eloisa päättää mahdollisten optioiden hankkimisesta vuoden 2028 loppuun mennessä. Sopimuskausi alkaa sopimuksen allekirjoittamisesta. Sopimus allekirjoitetaan mahdollisimman pian lainvoimaisen päätöksen jälkeen. Sopimus on toistaiseksi voimassa oleva. Laitteen tulee soveltua diffuusiokapasiteetin mittaamiseen ja spirometriatutkimusten tekemiseen. Spirometria ja diffuusiokapasiteetti ovat keskeisiä keuhkojen toimintakokeita. Spirometrialla mitataan keuhkojen tilavuutta ja ilman virtausta, mikä auttaa tunnistamaan ahtauttavat (esim. astma, COPD) tai rajoittavat keuhkosairaudet. Diffuusiokapasiteetti mittaa kaasujen siirtymistä keuhkorakkuloista vereen, ja sitä käytetään keuhkokudoksen sairauksien (esim. fibroosi) arvioinnissa. Laitteella tulee pystyä tekemään spirometria ja bronkodilataatiokoe, diffuusiokoe hengityslihasvoiman mittaus sekä SNIP. Pyydettäessä tarjoaja toimittaa kustannuksellaan tarjotun laitteistokokonaisuuden koekäyttöön Mikkelin keskussairaalalle. Tarjouspyyntö julkaistaan ehdollisena optioiden osalta: optioiden hankinnat voidaan toteuttaa, mikäli hankinnoille varatut investointimäärärahat hyväksytään.,

title: Market Research for Specialized Flight Test and Evaluation Training Services
description: 1. Purpose The Department of War (DoW) is conducting market research to identify interested and capable businesses that can provide test pilot training in support of the US Air Force Security Assistance Training (AFSAT) squadron. This Sources Sought Notice is issued for market research and planning purposes only. It does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quote, commitment by the Government, or promise to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government will not reimburse any costs associated with preparation or submission of a response. Responses will be used to assess market capability, commercial availability, acquisition alternatives, and the availability of small-business concerns capable of performing the anticipated requirement as a prime contractor. 2. Anticipated Requirement and Preliminary Training Demand The Government is seeking information from firms capable of providing flight-training services that may include: Flight instruction for test pilot training Ground-school instruction and courseware; Instructor pilots and, if applicable, simulator instructors; Aircraft, simulators, training devices, facilities, equipment, and associated support; Student scheduling, training administration, and records management; Evaluation, qualification, proficiency, or recurrent-training events; Safety management, quality assurance, and accident/incident reporting processes; Training status, student performance, and completion reporting; and Other associated services that are necessary to deliver the required training outcomes. 3. Required Course Offerings and Course-Specific Response Requirements Interested parties must demonstrate the capability to provide the entirety of the following courses and specialized curricula: Category Course Title Duration / Certification Professional Traditional Professional Course (NATO STANAG 4578 / SETP-Compliant Flight Test Qualification; EASA Part-FCL.820 Approved Category 1 (Lead Flight Test) and Category 2 Flight Test Rating Training via an authorized EASA Approved Training Organization (ATO)) 50 Weeks Professional Standard EASA Cat 1 Certified 31 Weeks Professional Traditional EASA Category 2 Course 20 Weeks Professional Performance and Flying Qualities Professional Course 26 Weeks Professional System Professional Course 26 Weeks Unmanned Systems UAV Systems Testing Specialized Short & Specialized Pre-TPS Course Short Course Short & Specialized Helmet Mounted Display (HMD) and Night Vision Goggle (NVG) Testing Short Course Short & Specialized Introduction to Systems Testing Short Course Short & Specialized Operational Test and Evaluation (OT&E) Course Short Course Short & Specialized EASA Approved Training Organization Upset Prevention and Recovery Training (UPRT) Short Course Short & Specialized Spin Training Course Short Course Short & Specialized Crew Resource Management for Flight Testers Short Course 4. Anticipated Mandatory Institutional Accreditations, Approvals, and Credentials The Government anticipates that a future solicitation may require the successful contractor to maintain the following institutional accreditations, approvals, and credentials. Respondents shall provide verifiable documentation of their current status, including the issuing organization, approval/accreditation number where applicable, scope, effective date, expiration date, and any pending renewal or limitation. Mandatory accreditations may be satisfied by the prime contractor, a joint venture partner, or a designated and formal subcontractor/teaming partner at time of proposal submission/prior to contract performance. 4.1 Collegiate Accreditation Accreditation as a degree-granting institution by an accrediting agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education, such as the WASC Senior College and University Commission (WSCUC), or another recognized accrediting agency. 4.2 Engineering-Program Accreditation Accreditation by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET) for a relevant Master of Science program. Response requested: Identify the applicable graduate program, ABET-accreditation status, and relationship of that program to the flight-test curriculum. 4.3 European Union Aviation Safety Agency Approval Status as a European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) Approved Training Organization (ATO) approved to provide flight-test training for issuance of EASA Category 1 and Category 2 flight-test ratings, as applicable to the proposed courses. Response requested: Provide the ATO approval and scope of privileges and identify the specific courses that support EASA Category 1 and/or Category 2 flight-test ratings. EASA rules describe the authority of approved training organizations to provide training for Category 1 or 2 flight-test ratings, with potential extension for other flight-test categories and personnel under specified conditions. 4.4 Federal Aviation Administration Air Agency Certificate An active Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Air Agency Certificate under Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR) Part 141 - Pilot Schools, including the applicable approval for pilot special preparation under Appendix K. Response requested: Provide the certificate number, current status, applicable approved courses, and any limitations relevant to the anticipated requirement. Preliminary training demand: Estimated students annually: 10-15 Estimated classes/training iterations annually: 10 Estimated flight hours, sorties, simulator hours, or other workload metric: Integrated live-fly, variable-stability, and synthetic simulation environment Anticipated period of performance: 5 years Anticipated start date: 1 Oct 2027 All quantities and dates are estimates for market research purposes and may change. For each course, respondents shall provide: A course description and current syllabus or curriculum summary; The basis for any stated certification, rating, or credential awarded upon course completion; Course duration, format, location, and maximum student capacity; Instructor qualifications and available aircraft, simulators, test assets, laboratories, and other instructional resources; Any prerequisites, minimum student qualifications, medical requirements, or flight-hour requirements; The number of times the course has been delivered within the preceding [insert timeframe]; and Any limitations, lead times, or dependencies affecting ability to provide the course. 5. Capability Statement Content Interested firms should submit a capability statement of no more than 10 pages, excluding cover page and attachments. The capability statement should include: Company information Legal business name UEI and CAGE code Business address Website, if available Primary business point of contact, using business contact information Proposed NAICS code(s) Business size and socioeconomic status under the proposed NAICS code Technical Capability and Past Performance Provide the course-specific capability information required by Section 3 and the accreditation, approval, and credential documentation required by Section 4. In addition, provide up to 3 examples of recent (last 3 years) and relevant (proven track record of similar work that demonstrates ability to deliver specified courses and services and possesses required accreditations) past performance including customer type, period of performance, scope, training volume, and complexity. Acquisition and Market Feedback Address whether the requirement is commercially available without material modification; recommended contract or ordering structure; principal cost, schedule, mobilization, and performance risks; and recommended outcome-based performance measures. Teaming and Subcontracting Identify whether the firm intends to perform as a prime contractor, subcontractor, or teaming partner, and identify the discrete functions it can perform. Structure capability submissions into functional tracks (e.g.) - Track A: Comprehensive Graduate TPS Curric

title: Katujen ja muiden yleisten alueiden talvikunnossapito
description: Ylivieskan kaupungin kuntatekniikan palvelut pyytää tarjouksia katu- ja muiden yleisten alueiden lumenauraukseen ja -poiskuljettamiseen sekä liukkaudentorjuntaan tarjouspyyntöasiakirjojen mukaisesti. Talvikunnossapitoon kuuluu katujen, kevyenliikenteen väylien, yleisten alueiden ja kaupungin kiinteistöjen lumen auraus sekä polanteen poisto, liukkaudentorjunta ja lumen pois kuljettaminen tarvittavilta osin. Tarjottavat talvikunnossapitokohteet on jaettu osahankintoihin liitteenä olevan karttamateriaalin mukaisesti. Talvikunnossapidon osa-alueita on yhteensä seitsemän (7) kpl. Osa-alueiden järjestys/nimeäminen poikkeaa numerojärjestyksestä hankintayksikön parhaaksi katsoman merkintätavan vuoksi. Edellä mainittujen lisäksi lumen poiskuljettaminen on eritelty omaksi osahankinnaksi. Tarjoaja voi antaa tarjouksen yhteen tai useampaan osa-alueeseen. Osatarjoukset osa-alueilla eivät ole mahdollisia, eli tarjoajan tulee tarjota molempia (aurausta ja liukkauden torjuntaa) tarjoamalleen osa-alueelle. Osahankinta-alue 10 poikkeaa muista talvikunnossapidon osa-alueista siten, että alueen tarjouskilpailun voittaneesta urakoitsijasta valitaan samalla koko talvihoidon ykkösurakoitsija. Ykkösurakoitsijan tehtävistä ja hinnoittelusta on kerrottu tarkemmin kohdassa "hankintaa tai osaa koskevat lisätiedot". Talvikunnossapidettävät kadut, kevyenliikenteen väylät, yleiset alueet ja kiinteistöt voivat muuttua sopimuskauden aikana. Sopimuskausi on yhden talvikunnossapitokauden (talvi 2026-2027) + mahdolliset optio talvikunnossapitokaudet (talvi 2027-2028) + (talvi 2028-2029). Sopimuksen arvioitu aloitusaika on 2026 vuoden alkutalvi. Hankintayksikkö voi tarjota tarjouskilpailun voittaneille urakoitsijoille, heidän tarjoamillaan tuntihinnoilla, myös erikseen tilattavia talvikunnossapitotöitä urakka-alueen ulkopuolella. Hankintayksikkö pidättää oikeuden teettää tuntitöitä myös urakoitsijoilla, jotka eivät tule tarjouskilpailussa valituiksi urakoitsijoiksi., Alue 1 - Keskusta Vaadittava kalusto: Kolme (3) aurausyksikköä ja kaksi (2) hiekoitinta. Aurauskalusto: Kalusto 1: Traktori, aura ja raspi. Kalusto 2: Traktori, aura ja alaterä. Kalusto 3: Traktori, traktorikaivuri tai pyöräkuormaaja ja aura. Liukkauden torjunta kalusto: Kalusto 1: Vaunuhiekoitin 2,5-4 kuutiota. Kalusto 2: Hiekoitin 1,5-4 kuutiota. Osa-alueen aluerajaus on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä. Alueelle sisältyvät kiinteistöt: • Terveyskeskus, Kirkkotie 4 • Kaupungintalo + paikoitus, Kyöstintie 4 • Kirjasto, Kyöstintie 4 • Kasarmin alue, Rautatiekatu 12,14 • Päivärinnan koulu, Koulukatu 2 • Musiikkitalo Akustiikka, Koulukatu 2B, Alue 3 - Koskipuhto, Lundinkangas Vaadittava kalusto: Kaksi (2) aurausyksikköä ja kaksi (2) hiekoitinta. Aurauskalusto: Kalusto 1: Traktori, aura ja raspi. Kalusto 2: Traktori, aura ja alaterä. Liukkauden torjunta kalusto: Kalusto 1: Vaunuhiekoitin 2,5-4 kuutiota. Kalusto 2: Saa käyttöön kaupungin kolmen (3) kuution vaunuhiekoittimen. Osa-alueen aluerajaus on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä. Alueelle sisältyvät kiinteistöt: • Toimintakeskus Kipinä, Suopellontie 6 • Katajan koulut, Katajantie 23 • Suvannon urheilutalo, Koskipuhdontie 28, Alue 4 - Kivioja, Hakalahti, Niemenranta, Männistö Vaadittava kalusto: Kaksi (2) aurausyksikköä ja kaksi (2) hiekoitinta. Aurauskalusto: Kalusto 1: Traktori, aura ja raspi. Kalusto 2: Traktori, aura ja raspi. Liukkauden torjunta kalusto: Kalusto 1: Vaunuhiekoitin 2,5-4 kuutiota. Kalusto 2: Saa käyttää kaupungin kahdeksan (8) kuution vaihto- tai koukkulavakärryn päälle vedettävää hiekoitinta. Urakoitsijalta vaaditaan oma kärry, mihin hiekoitin voidaan ottaa kyytiin. Osa-alueen aluerajaus on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä. Alueelle sisältyvät kiinteistöt: • Hakalahden päiväkoti, Takkulantie 1 • Matleena-Mielikki, Katajistontie 10 • Paloasema, Jokilaaksojen pelastuslaitos, Puusepäntie 2 • Niemelän koulu, Niemelänkyläntie 353 • Kiviojan koulu, Kiviojantie 16 • Rahkolan koulu + parkkialue, Hakalahdenkatu 8 • Lukio, Takkulantie 3 • Pieneläinklinikka, Katajistontie 2, Alue 6 - Kaisaniemi, Hollihaka Vaadittava kalusto: Kaksi (2) aurausyksikköä ja yksi (1) hiekoitin. Aurauskalusto: Kalusto 1: Traktori, aura ja raspi. Kalusto 2: Traktori, aura ja raspi. Liukkauden torjunta kalusto: Kalusto 1: Vaunuhiekoitin 2,5-4 kuutiota. Osa-alueen aluerajaus on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä. Alueelle sisältyvät kiinteistöt: • Sipilän palvelukeskus, Visalantie 300 • Sipilän vanha asuinrakennus, Visalantie 302 • Simonpuiston päiväkoti, Kantotie 5 • Joukahaisen päiväkoti, Pakolankatu 23 • Rannan koulut, Lampintie 23 • Kaisaniemen koulu + jättöalue, Mäntytie 2, Alue 9- Toivonpuisto, Puuhkala, Koivukallio, Salmiperä Vaadittava kalusto: Kaksi (2) aurausyksikköä ja yksi (1) hiekoitin. Aurauskalusto: Kalusto 1: Traktori, aura ja raspi. Kalusto 2: Traktori, aura ja raspi. Liukkauden torjunta kalusto: Kalusto 1: Vaunuhiekoitin 2,5-4 kuutiota. Osa-alueen aluerajaus on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä. Alueelle sisältyvät kiinteistöt: • Ojakylänkoulu, Perkkiöntie 50 • Liikuntakeskus, Närhitie 2 • Jäähalli, Närhitie 2 • Urheilukentän huoltorakennus, Närhitie 2 • Liikuntapuiston huoltorakennus, Salmiperäntie 8 • Safarin huoltorakennus (tarvittaessa tilaajan ilmoituksesta) Salmiperäntie 1, Alue 10 - Pyörreperä, Savari + ykkösurakoitsijan tehtävät Vaadittava kalusto: Yksi (1) aurausyksikköä ja yksi (1) hiekoitin. Aurauskalusto: Kalusto 1: Traktori, aura ja alaterä. Liukkauden torjunta kalusto: Kalusto 1: Vaunuhiekoitin 2,5-4 kuutiota. Osa-alueen aluerajaus on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä. Alueelle sisältyvät kiinteistöt: • Keskuskeittiö Vilja, Puhurinkatu 11 Työtehtäviin kuluvat osa-alueen talvikunnossapitotöiden lisäksi myös ykkösurakoitsijan tehtävät ja vastuut., Alue 20 - Raudaskylä, Vähäkangas Vaadittava kalusto: Yksi (1) aurausyksikköä ja yksi (1) hiekoitin. Aurauskalusto: Kalusto 1: Traktori, aura ja raspi. Liukkauden torjunta kalusto: Kalusto 1: Vaunuhiekoitin 2,5-4 kuutiota. Osa-alueen aluerajaus on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä. Alueelle sisältyvät kiinteistöt: • Raudaskosken koulu, Raudaskoskentie 7 • Vähäkankaan koulu, Vähänkankaantie 622 • Huhmarkallio / Kisamajat, Huhmarintie, Lumen kuljetus Lumen kuljetus kaupungin osoittamalle lumen läjitysalueelle.,

description: Η δημοπρατούμενη σύμβαση, για λόγους επίτευξης καλύτερου λειτουργικού αποτελέσματος, είναι και δημοπρατείται ως σύμβαση «με το κλειδί στο χέρι» (turn-key project), υπό την έννοια ότι ο Ανάδοχος αναλαμβάνει στο πλαίσιο των αναλυτικών προδιαγραφών και λειτουργικών απαιτήσεων της παρούσας να παραδώσει κάθε έναν από τους δώδεκα (12) συρμούς έξι (6) οχημάτων της σειράς Ι, δηλαδή συνολικά εβδομήντα δύο (72) οχήματα, πλήρως αναβαθμισμένα, με διάρκεια ζωής (service life) 25 χρόνια από την ολοκλήρωση της σύμβασης. Συνοπτικά το αντικείμενο περιλαμβάνει σύμφωνα με τους όρους του συνόλου των συμβατικών τευχών: Α1) Την εκπόνηση της Μελέτης. Α2) Την αναβάθμιση, δοκιμή και θέση σε λειτουργία δώδεκα (12) συρμών, των έξι (6) οχημάτων εκάστου με ονομαστική τάση λειτουργίας 750Vdc. Α3) Την προμήθεια των ειδικών εργαλείων, του διαγνωστικού εξοπλισμού δοκιμών και ομοιώματος, όπως αυτά ορίζονται στη Σύμβαση. Α4) Την τριετή εγγύηση καλής λειτουργίας των συρμών και την προμήθεια των ανταλλακτικών και αναλώσιμων ανταλλακτικών της περιόδου θέσης σε λειτουργία, καθώς και των ανταλλακτικών και αναλώσιμων ανταλλακτικών της περιόδου εγγύησης που απαιτούνται για τις περιόδους αυτές. Α5) Την σύνταξη και υποβολή των τευχών τεκμηρίωσης, των εγχειριδίων συντήρησης και λειτουργίας και των εικονογραφημένων καταλόγων ανταλλακτικών. Α6) Την εκπαίδευση του προσωπικού της ΣΤΑΣΥ. B) Την προμήθεια των ανταλλακτικών αρχικής υποστήριξης, όπως αναλυτικά περιλαμβάνονται στο συνημμένο στο έντυπο οικονομικής προσφοράς «Πίνακας Ανταλλακτικών Αρχικής Υποστήριξης». Οι ως άνω απαιτούμενες προμήθειες και υπηρεσίες, καθώς και οι αναλυτικές τους τεχνικές προδιαγραφές περιγράφονται στο τεύχος των Τεχνικών Προδιαγραφών (εφεξής ΤΠ). Τα προς προμήθεια είδη κατατάσσονται στους ακόλουθους κωδικούς του Κοινού Λεξιλογίου για τις Δημόσιες Συμβάσεις (CPV) : • 34622100-4 Επιβατικά βαγόνια αστικού σιδηροδρόμου. • 34630000-2 Μέρη σιδηροδρομικών ή τροχιοδρομικών μηχανών έλξης ή τροχαίου υλικού· εξοπλισμός ελέγχου της κυκλοφορίας για σιδηροδρόμους. • 50222000-7 Υπηρεσίες επισκευής και συντήρησης τροχαίου εξοπλισμού. Η εκτιμώμενη αξία της σύμβασης ανέρχεται στο ποσό των εκατόν εννέα εκατομμυρίων ευρώ (109.000.000 €) μη συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ. Ο προϋπολογισμός αναλύεται ως εξής: Α) Για τα ανωτέρω υπ’ αρίθμ. Α1 έως Α6, ποσό εκατόν έξι εκατομμύρια πεντακόσιες χιλιάδες Ευρώ (106.500.000€) χωρίς ΦΠΑ. Β) Για τα ανωτέρω υπ’ αρίθμ. Β, ποσό δύο εκατομμυρίων και πεντακοσίων χιλιάδων Ευρώ (2.500.000) χωρίς ΦΠΑ Επισημαίνεται ότι οι οικονομικές προσφορές που θα δοθούν δεν θα υπερβαίνουν το συνολικό προϋπολογισμό, αλλά ούτε και τους επιμέρους προϋπολογισμούς των ανωτέρω πεδίων (Α) και (Β).

title: Germany – General management consultancy services – Beratungsleistungen zur Konzeption und Einführung eines integrierten Unternehmenssteuerungssystems
description: Die Verwaltungsdirektion des WDR beabsichtigt, einen Rahmenvertrag über Beratungs-, Konzeptions- und fachliche Begleitleistungen für das Projekt "Business Warehouse" abzuschließen. Das Vorhaben ist als mehrjähriges Transformations- und Umsetzungsprojekt angelegt. Ziel des Projekts ist die fachliche Konzeption und schrittweise Einführung eines integrierten Steuerungsmodells, das strategische Planung, Mittelallokation, Portfolio- und Performancebetrachtung sowie Transparenz über Ressourcen, Kosten und Wirkung miteinander verknüpft. Das Vorhaben dient damit der Weiterentwicklung der unternehmensweiten Steuerungsfähigkeit des WDR. Der Auftragnehmer begleitet das Vorhaben von der Feinkonzeption über die Umsetzungsphase bis zur Produktivsetzung und dem Übergang in den Regelbetrieb. Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung sind ausschließlich Beratungsleistungen, die fachliche Konzeption sowie die fachliche Begleitung des Projekts über alle Projektphasen hinweg. Erwartet wird auch die fachliche Konzeption und Begleitung der technischen Umsetzung sowie die Übersetzung fachlicher Anforderungen in umsetzbare Prozess-, Daten- und Systemanforderungen. Die technische Implementierung und Softwareentwicklung selbst sind nicht Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung. Der Auftrag wird als Rahmenvertrag ohne Abnahmeverpflichtung ausgeschrieben. Die Vertragslaufzeit beträgt 27 Monate ab Leistungsbeginn; der WDR erhält die Option, den Ver-trag einmalig um ein weiteres Jahr zu verlängern. Die geschätzte Abrufmenge beträgt ca. 350 Personentage; die Höchstmenge beträgt 400 Personentage. Mit Erreichen der Höchstmenge endet die Möglichkeit weiterer Abrufe aus dem Rahmenvertrag. Aus der geschätzten Abrufmenge folgt keine Verpflichtung des WDR, Leistungen in diesem Umfang abzurufen.
